subject: relationships
topic: The 'mere exposure' effect makes you like people you shouldn't
angle: While familiarity can increase acceptance of foods and influence investment choices, social associations are distinct from simple stimulus familiarity and can actively modify perception.
title: The Bias of Familiarity

hooks.text: Do you like them because they are familiar?
You assume repetition builds trust. The evidence shows it modifies perception.
You are letting familiarity bias your investments.
A coffee cup on a desk.

reveal.headline: Social associations are distinct from simple repeated exposure.
reveal.body: Social association can modify perception and alter expectancies automatically. This is not the same as simply seeing something many times.

explain.headline: Familiarity influences your choices.
explain.body: Investors show a familiarity bias when choosing companies. Familiarity with novel foods is linked to higher acceptance. However, these influences are not always synonymous with repeated exposure.

matters.headline: Your perception may be biased.
matters.body: That may be why you favor certain choices. Your brain may prioritize what is familiar over what is optimal, automatically modifying how you see the world.

example.headline: The office chair.
example.body: You sit in the same chair every morning. You choose the same brand of coffee. These habits shape how you perceive your daily routine.

question.headline: What are you choosing because it is familiar?

stat.label: how social association affects your brain

claims.text: Social association does not reflect stimulus familiarity per se, that it can modify perception, that it can both occur automatically and alter expectancies.
claims.quote: Evidence using this procedure suggests that social association does not reflect stimulus familiarity per se, that it can modify perception, that it can both occur automatically and alter expectancies

claims.text: Judgements of inefficient actions were biased towards the efficient prediction.
claims.quote: Judgements of inefficient actions were biased towards the efficient prediction (straight trajectories upward to avoid the obstruction, arched trajectories downward towards the target).

claims.text: Investors do exhibit familiarity bias when choosing between different companies to invest in.
claims.quote: The results of this exploratory study indicate that investors do exhibit familiarity bias when choosing between different companies to invest in.

claims.text: Familiarity with novel foods and curiosity both led to higher acceptance.

verdict: The evidence shows that familiarity and social associations influence perception and decision-making, but they are not always synonymous with simple repeated exposure.
caveat: The sources do not provide direct evidence on the 'mere exposure' effect specifically regarding the development of trust or intimacy in human relationships.
caption:
Familiarity shapes your perception of the world.

Research shows that social associations can automatically modify your expectancies, though these findings are not synonymous with simple repeated exposure. The evidence does not provide direct data on how this affects trust or intimacy in human relationships.
